title: Framework has no zeroization backstop for provider ctx
description:
At fd_release, the framework calls ops->sess_free(ctx) / key_free(ctx) and trusts the provider to call memzero_explicit before kfree. The framework has no backstop: state->ctx is a void* of unknown size, so the framework cannot independently zeroize it. inbuf and outbuf are framework-owned and zeroized independently; ctx is not.

All 11 current providers comply with the contract (crypto2dev_provider.h line 133-135 / 450-453). The risk is future providers that omit memzero_explicit — there is no runtime detection and no second line of defense.

Fix: add size_t ctx_size to struct crypto2dev_algo_ops. Rename sess_free to sess_cleanup (frees internal allocations only, does NOT kfree ctx). Framework then does memzero_explicit(ctx, ops->ctx_size) + kfree(ctx) after sess_cleanup returns. Order is mandatory: sess_cleanup must run first so internal heap pointers (e.g. GCM ctx->aad, ctx->inbuf) are freed before the top-level ctx is overwritten. Same change for key_free -> key_cleanup + key_ctx_size.

Same analysis applies to key_ctx.
close_reason: Design decision: framework trusts providers to zeroize ctx. The contract in crypto2dev_provider.h (sess_free line 133-135, key_free line 450-453) explicitly requires memzero_explicit before kfree. Splitting sess_free into sess_cleanup + framework-level zero+kfree would require tracking ctx_size and holding the allocation alive longer — memory pressure not justified. Enforcement is contract + code review + audit. All current providers comply.
